head: Wall Street ignored
the small investor.
slides.sub: One broker built a business on them.

image.label: A lone office worker reading stock prices in a 1970s city
image.brief: 1970년대 미국 도시 거리, 신문 주식 시세면을 읽는 평범한 직장인의 실루엣. 뒤로 고층 금융가 빌딩. 따뜻한 필름 톤. 실제 로고 없음.

head: Every broker charged
the same price.
body: For most of the 20th century, US stock brokers charged fixed commissions. Whether you bought a few shares or a huge block, the rates were set, not competed on.
For ordinary people, buying stock was expensive, and brokers had little reason to court them.

image.label: A crowded 1970s brokerage floor with paper tickets
image.brief: 1970년대 증권사 객장. 종이 주문표, 전화기, 정장 차림의 브로커들. 인물은 일반적인 모습, 얼굴은 흐릿하게.

slides.label: the day US regulators ended fixed commissions, known as May Day
body: After that, brokers could charge what they liked. Many big firms cut prices for large institutional clients. For small investors, prices often went up instead.

image.label: A calendar page marked May 1 on a desk
image.brief: 1970년대 사무실 책상 위 5월 1일 달력 한 장과 전화기. 긴장감 있는 아침 빛.

head: A small firm in
San Francisco.
body: Charles Schwab ran a modest brokerage, far from Wall Street. He saw what May Day opened up: millions of people who picked their own stocks and didn't want to pay for advice they never used.

image.label: A small office with a view of San Francisco hills
image.brief: 1970년대 샌프란시스코 언덕이 보이는 작은 사무실. 책상 몇 개와 전화기. 실존 인물 얼굴 없이 뒷모습 실루엣.

head: Prices are now free.
What do you build?
body: You run a small brokerage. The big firms have research teams, famous names and armies of brokers.

options.text: Offer full service with research and advice, just a bit cheaper
options.feedback: You keep the costs of a big firm without its brand. Hard to win on price that way. Keep swiping.

options.text: Chase big institutional clients, where the trading volume is
options.feedback: That's where the giants were fighting hardest, with deep relationships. Keep swiping.

options.text: Drop advice entirely and sell cheap, simple trades to individuals
options.feedback: You give up the clients who want hand-holding, and the fees that come with them. Keep swiping.

image.label: Three doors in a marble lobby
image.brief: 대리석 로비에 나란히 선 세 개의 문. 1970년대 금융가 분위기.

head: No advice.
No sales pitch.
body: Schwab chose the stripped-down path. It executed trades at low prices and skipped the research and stock tips.
Its brokers were paid salaries, not commissions, so they had no reason to push customers into extra trades. That became part of the pitch.

image.label: A broker on the phone taking a simple order
image.brief: 전화로 간단한 주문을 받는 1970년대 브로커. 책상 위 주문표 한 장. 차분한 분위기, 얼굴은 일반적인 모습.

head: Cheap, but not
faceless.
body: Schwab opened branches so customers could walk in, and put his own face in ads to show a real person stood behind the firm.
It also spent heavily on computers early, so low prices didn't mean slow or sloppy trades.

image.label: A storefront branch office on a 1980s main street
image.brief: 1980년대 미국 소도시 거리의 작은 증권 지점 외관. 실제 간판·로고 없음. 큰 유리창, 안에 고객 몇 명.

head: Bought by a bank,
then bought back.
body: Bank of America acquired the firm in 1983. The fit proved awkward, and in 1987 Schwab and other managers bought the company back, then took it public that same year.
By then, discount brokerage was a mainstream way for Americans to invest.

image.label: Two hands exchanging a key over a contract
image.brief: 계약서 위로 열쇠를 건네는 두 손. 1980년대 회의실. 인물 얼굴 없음.

head: Serve who they ignore,
in a way they can't copy.
body: Full-service firms earned their money from commission brokers and advice. Matching Schwab's model meant attacking their own business, so most didn't.
Schwab won by serving one segment well: self-directed investors who wanted low prices and honest execution, nothing more.

image.label: A small arrow slipping past a large wall
image.brief: 거대한 벽 옆 좁은 틈으로 빠져나가는 작은 화살표 그래픽. 금융가 색감.

head: When the rules change,
ask who gets overcharged.
body: A new rule or technology often helps big players first. The customers left behind can become your whole market.
**Try it today:** which customers pay for things they never use? What could you remove to serve them better?

image.label: A single stock ticker glowing in a dark room
image.brief: 어두운 방 안에서 홀로 빛나는 주식 시세판. 차분하고 희망적인 톤. 로고 없음.

factChecks.note: 1975년 5월 1일 SEC가 증권 거래 고정 수수료를 폐지했다는 사실(일명 'May Day')은 SEC 자료와 당시 보도로 확인하세요. → [2026-11-02 확인] 1975년 5월 1일 SEC 고정 수수료 폐지 확인.
고정 수수료 폐지 후 대형 증권사들이 기관 고객 수수료는 낮추고 소액 개인 고객 수수료는 올렸다는 내용은 여러 기록에 나오지만 회사별 사실은 단정하지 않았습니다. 카드에는 'many big firms'로만 적었습니다.
Schwab이 1975년 할인 중개 서비스를 시작했고, 브로커에게 수수료 대신 급여를 지급하며 투자 조언을 하지 않았다는 점은 Charles Schwab 공식 연혁과 Schwab의 자서전으로 확인하세요.
Bank of America 인수(1981년 발표, 1983년 완료)와 1987년 경영진 재인수, 같은 해 상장은 회사 연혁 기준입니다. 인수·재인수 금액은 넣지 않았습니다. → [2026-11-02 확인] 1981년 합의, 1983년 Bank of America 인수 완료, 1987년 경영진 재인수와 같은 해 9월 상장 확인.
지점 확대, Charles Schwab 본인의 얼굴을 쓴 광고, 초기 컴퓨터 시스템 투자는 회사 연혁과 언론 보도에 나옵니다. 지점 수·고객 수 같은 숫자는 넣지 않았습니다.
1987년 주가 폭락 이후 영향 등 기간 말 실적 수치는 확인이 어려워 넣지 않았습니다. 성공은 정성 표현으로만 썼습니다.
